newsitem.title: JAPAN: EPA says doesn't think economic trend has changed.
newsitem.headline: EPA says doesn't think economic trend has changed.

text.p: Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Friday that the did not think the general trend of the Japanese economy has changed drastically since the release of the "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment last week.

Asked whether the current Japanese market reflected the country's economic fundamentals, Aso said markets do not necessarily reflect economic fundamentals as has been seen in currency movements over the past few years.
"The yen was at 79 yen to the dollar when the Japanese economy was worse than it is now and the yen was at 113 yen to the dollar even after the economy had improved considerably.
"These show that markets do not necessarily move along with the economic reality."
Aso said the same can be said for the stock market.
"We are not so pessimistic about the economy," he said.
Aso said the negative effect of the sales tax rise on car purchases was expected to have been limited to the April to June period.
The limited impact of the sales tax rise on car purchases was what the EPA had expected, he said.
